newsitem.title: SPAIN: Peseta debt/interbank market closing report.
newsitem.headline: Peseta debt/interbank market closing report.

text.p: Spanish government bonds closed almost unchanged on Monday after a technical day's trading which saw bonos start higher, turn negative and then positive again.
With no domestic news in sight dealers said Spanish bonds moved in line with other European markets, especially Italian BTPs, depressed by a statement by a Bundesbank council member.
Klaus-Dieter Kuehbacher said Italy should not take part in the European single currency from the start in 1999.
"The market is taking a more cautious approach towards EMU convergence," a dealer in Madrid said. The 10-year spread over German Bunds rose to 182 basis points from 179.
Futures saw little volume although the cash market was more active, particularly in the ten year segment, one dealer said. Next Wednesday the Treasury will tender 10-year bonds and six-month bills.
After a bull run which has lasted weeks, bonos are now looking for direction. But there are still uncertainties.
"The Spanish market is resting a little," Gregorio Gomez at All Trading in Madrid said. "It is very likely preparing for a faster move, but it's really hard to say in which direction."
